title: Criteria to evaluate neurogenic bladder in patients with Congenital Zika Syndrome
author: Lucia Maria Costa Monteiro
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k5vcy66
materials: Inspection of abdomen: bladder and bowel
Second phase of the urological screening:
Further investigation of the urological system:
Bladder pressure is measured before emptying the bladder
Leak point pressure is measured at first leak
Voiding pressure is measured when void starts.
EMG was performed using patch EMG electrodes
Third phase of the urological screening:
ureteral or pelvic dilatation at renal US

steps.title: Refer children for urological assessment
steps.instruction: Refer every child with confirmed Congenital Zika Syndrome to a pediatric urology service for evaluation.

steps.title: Conduct initial assessment
steps.instruction: Obtain a detailed clinical history, perform a comprehensive physical examination, and collect urine for urinalysis and culture.

steps.title: Gather prenatal and maternal history
steps.instruction: Ask about maternal rash, low‑grade fever, myalgia, arthralgia, fatigue, conjunctival hyperemia during pregnancy, gestational timing of Zika exposure, and any perinatal complications.

steps.title: Assess bladder habits
steps.instruction: Record number of diapers used per day, wetness of diapers, interval between changes (continence interval), and inquire about UTI symptoms such as urine colour change, turbidity, fever, and dysuria.

steps.title: Assess bowel habits
steps.instruction: Document daily water intake, diet type, any special bowel‑emptying regimen, frequency of bowel movements, and stool characteristics using the Bristol Stool Scale.

steps.title: Perform physical examination
steps.instruction: Carry out a systemic exam, measure head circumference to confirm microcephaly, inspect spine and upper/lower extremities for irregularities, and test perineal sensation and reflexes.

steps.title: Obtain urine sample via catheter
steps.instruction: Collect urine for urinalysis and culture during the initial visit and at every febrile episode using urethral catheterization.

substeps.instruction: Apply topical lidocaine gel (1%) to the urethra.
Use a double‑lumen pediatric catheter for collection.

steps.title: Order basic laboratory tests
steps.instruction: If not already performed at CZS screening, order a complete blood count (CBC), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and serum creatinine.

steps.title: Perform urinary ultrasonography
steps.instruction: Evaluate kidneys, ureters, and bladder:

substeps.instruction: Kidneys: assess length, outline, cortico‑medullary differentiation, and calyceal/pelvic dilatation; pelvic transverse diameter ≤ 7 mm in neonates and ≤ 10 mm in older children; note any renal dilatation.
Ureters: look for longitudinal and transverse dilatation.
Bladder: perform pre‑void assessment (wall, contents, volume) and, when possible, post‑void residual (PVR) measurement.

steps.title: Conduct urodynamic study (UDS)
steps.instruction: After ruling out UTI, perform cystometry (CMG) using a double‑lumen pediatric catheter under topical lidocaine 1% anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Measure initial residual volume (consider diaper wetness or voiding during catheterization).
Calculate filling rate as 5 %–10 % of the expected bladder capacity for age (ml/min).
Infuse fluid until just before voiding; record maximum bladder capacity when baseline pressure exceeds 40 cm H₂O or infused volume reaches 1.5 × expected capacity.
Record maximum bladder pressure at that capacity.
Measure post‑void residual (PVR) at the end of the exam.
When possible, obtain pressure measurements outside any bladder contraction for baseline values.

steps.title: Classify bladder behavior
steps.instruction: Assign the bladder to one of four categories based on UDS findings:

substeps.instruction: Normal bladder – relaxed during filling, sustained contraction at maximum capacity, relaxed sphincter, complete emptying without PVR.
Underactive bladder – relaxed during filling and unable to generate/maintain contraction for complete emptying.
Overactive bladder – detrusor contractions during filling, elevated intravesical pressures, early emptying before maximum capacity.
Low compliance bladder – loss of ability to stay relaxed during filling, progressive pressure rise, elevated pressures, early emptying.

steps.title: Record sphincter EMG activity
steps.instruction: Document sphincter electromyography during filling and voiding:

substeps.instruction: Normal (detrusor‑sphincter synergy): sphincter activity present during filling and reduces after high bladder pressure, leak, or voiding.
Detrusor‑sphincter dyssynergia (DSD): sphincter fails to relax or increases activity during high bladder pressure, leak, or voiding.

steps.title: Prepare child‑friendly environment
steps.instruction: Set up a room with toys, video/television showing children’s films; allow both parents to stay throughout the procedure to comfort the child.

steps.title: Prescribe anticholinergic medication
steps.instruction: Give chloridrate of oxybutynin (or another anticholinergic) to control overactive bladder and low bladder compliance.

steps.title: Initiate clean intermittent catheterization (CIC)
steps.instruction: Start CIC when bladder emptying is ineffective, recurrent UTIs occur, renal/ureteral dilatation is present, or grade 4–5 vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is detected.

substeps.instruction: Train parents using a specialized nurse; the nurse provides ongoing follow‑up.

steps.title: Administer antibiotics
steps.instruction: Treat confirmed urinary tract infections with antibiotics selected according to susceptibility testing; provide prophylactic antibiotics when history indicates recurrent UTIs.

steps.title: Perform voiding cystourethrography (VCUG)
steps.instruction: Obtain VCUG to assess bladder and urethral anatomy and to detect vesicoureteral reflux.

steps.title: Perform DMSA renal scan
steps.instruction: Order a DMSA scan to evaluate renal morphology, detect scarring, and identify pyelonephritis.

steps.title: Schedule regular clinical re‑evaluation
steps.instruction: Re‑evaluate the patient every 3–6 months, depending on risk factors and treatment response; advise parents to seek care if urine colour or smell changes or if fever occurs without known cause.

steps.title: Repeat UDS and renal/bladder ultrasound
steps.instruction: Repeat urodynamic studies and renal/bladder ultrasound every 6 months to 1 year, according to individual risk factors.
